territorial_scope.description: California statute applying to generative AI systems or services made publicly available to Californians, regardless of where the developer is located.

evidence.quote: is made publicly available to Californians for use

summary.short: Requires developers of generative AI systems made publicly available to Californians to post on their websites documentation of their training data, on or before January 1, 2026 and before each later release or substantial modification. Exempts certain security, aviation and defense systems.
summary.long: Adds Title 15.2 (Sections 3110 and 3111) to the Civil Code. Section 3110 defines artificial intelligence, developer, generative artificial intelligence, substantial modification, synthetic data generation and training of a generative AI system. Section 3111 requires a developer of a generative AI system or service released on or after January 1, 2022 that is made publicly available to Californians for use to post on its website documentation of the data used to train it. The posting duty applies on or before January 1, 2026 and before each later release or substantial modification. The documentation must include a high-level summary of the datasets: sources or owners, how they further the intended purpose, approximate number of data points, types of data points, whether they include copyright, trademark or patent protected data or are entirely public domain, whether they were purchased or licensed, whether they include personal information or aggregate consumer information, any cleaning or modification, the collection period, first-use dates, and any use of synthetic data generation. Exempt are systems whose sole purpose is security and integrity, systems whose sole purpose is operating aircraft in the national airspace, and systems developed for national security, military or defense purposes and made available only to a federal entity. The provided text contains no penalty or enforcement provision.
